digests.title: TLDR Tech — 2026-09-01
digests.tagline: Tim Cook's farewell 👋, FTC sues Amazon ⚖️, OpenClaw 2.0 🦞

stories.headline: FTC Sues Amazon, Alleging It Deceived Advertisers and Drove Up Prices (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: The FTC has filed a lawsuit against Amazon alleging that it manipulated prices that businesses paid to advertise on its retail platform. Amazon allegedly deceived advertisers by secretly raising the minimum price advertisers had to pay. Amazon's digital-ad platform is the third-largest in the world behind Google's and Meta's platforms. It earned $68 billion from ads in 2025.

stories.headline: Apple's Cook Says He ‘Will Miss This Work' in Final Memo as CEO (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Despite saying he'll miss the role of chief executive officer, Tim Cook has enormous comfort in the leadership of John Ternus, his replacement. Cook took over as Apple's CEO in August 2011. His 15-year tenure included the launch of the Apple Watch, AirPods, and major expansions to the iPhone, iPad, and Mac lines. Cook will remain as executive chairman, where his role will include working with governments around the world.

stories.headline: Lachy Groom backs Indian startup aiming to keep aircraft aloft for a year (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Alteon, a Bengaluru startup, aims to keep an aircraft in the sky for more than a year by harvesting energy from ocean winds. Its small, fixed-wing autonomous aircraft can extract energy from wind shear above the ocean through dynamic soaring. While the startup has yet to demonstrate an aircraft that can actually sustain flight using energy harvested through dynamic soaring, its 20-person team is building four to five aircraft a week for testing and has conducted more than 200 test flights in the past 30 days.

stories.headline: How Matic got robots into 10,000 homes (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Matic didn't grow by taking shortcuts. The company took six to seven years to ship, picked a category with very little new innovation, and spent most of that time on problems that don't demo well. It took on a market that already existed, put a different spin on it, and is now shipping American-made consumer home robots at real scale. This post looks at seven core lessons learned from Matic's journey so far.

stories.headline: The Future Tech Role Is the Product Architect (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Coding is moving from humans to agents. The human role is moving towards what should be built, defining how systems should work, and verifying results. The person deciding what should exist also needs to understand the system in which it will run. The product architect role owns the whole loop - it involves understanding the problem, deciding on a solution, designing the system, setting constraints, directing agents, and verifying what gets built.

stories.headline: OpenClaw 2.0, Accidentally (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: The OpenClaw 2.0 update touches every part of OpenClaw and includes a long tail of fixes. It took nearly two months to ship as the team was growing and the increased volume and pace of work outgrew the team's processes. OpenClaw remains open source and belongs to the people who use it and help build it. A link to the full release notes containing details of the over 16,000 pull requests merged in the release is available in the post.

stories.headline: Product Manager, Applied AI at TLDR ($200k base + $60k bonus, Fully Remote)
stories.blurb: TLDR is hiring its first PM to help build the agent-first operating layer used across the company. We're looking for a builder who has shipped real products/systems with LLMs. Click here to learn more .

stories.headline: Invisible Companies (22 minute read)
stories.blurb: Invisible companies remain invisible primarily because no one is paying attention to them. There are several reasons this could happen: they could be unknown, data about their existence or profitability is private, missing, or obscure, they are misunderstood, or they are disdained. Over time, the market should make these invisible companies visible, but that's not what happens. Thinking about invisible companies means thinking about strategy in a new way.

stories.headline: Google Has Removed Manifest V2 Extensions From the Chrome Web Store, Including uBlock Origin (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: All remaining Manifest V2 extensions have been removed from the Chrome Web Store. Manifest V2 extensions installed on Chrome 138 or earlier will remain installed. However, they will be unable to receive any updates and cannot be reinstalled from the Chrome Web Store once removed from Chrome. Users will no longer be able to find or install Manifest V2 extensions through the Chrome Web Store even if the Chromium-based browser they use continues to support Manifest V2.

stories.headline: Google is making AI Overviews even bigger on some search queries (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google will automatically fully expand AI Overviews in some search queries, effectively turning the whole page into an AI response.

stories.headline: There is no such thing as full decentralization (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: There's always an axis that centralizes.

stories.headline: Not Everyone Needs Superintelligence (17 minute read)
stories.blurb: Not everyone needs frontier models, and cheaper models are getting better and better anyway.

stories.headline: AI and Employment: So Far, So Good (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Most businesses report no change in total employment since the introduction of generative AI.

stories.headline: Anthropic Signs $35 Billion Cloud Deal Backed by Nvidia (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic has signed a cloud-computing deal with Lambda, which is backed by Nvidia, with Nvidia itself holding the lease on the data center.

stories.headline: Apple reveals ‘shocking evidence' from ex-employee's MacBook in OpenAI suit (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: The MacBook is evidence that Apple's trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed.

stories.headline: OpenClaw 2.0 (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenClaw released its largest update to date after an effort to simplify installation and rebuild its browser experience expanded into a broader overhaul. OpenClaw 2.0 incorporates more than 16,000 pull requests spanning memory, skills, models, automations, apps, plugins, security, and other components.

stories.headline: Introducing Solaris (17 minute read)
stories.blurb: Solaris is an Interface World Model. It can generate real-time interactive interfaces frame by frame as users interact with it. Solaris handles rendering and interactions jointly, generating every frame and every response to user input, eliminating the need for an intermediate representation. The model opens up new ways of building websites, apps, and other online interfaces. It can also be used to train agents in much more dynamic environments.

stories.headline: Muse Code (Website)
stories.blurb: Muse Code is a coding agent for the terminal and CI. It can plan, edit, and run commands to do tasks within projects. Approvals and an OS sandbox are on by default. Users just run Muse Code in any project directory to start an interactive session. Muse Spark is now available on the Meta Model API and Muse Code.

stories.headline: A deep dive into ZCode (17 minute read)
stories.blurb: ZCode is Z.ai's desktop coding agent. Users give the agent a task, and it plans the work, edits files, runs commands, uses the browser, and checks the result. Tasks can be run in parallel, and users can schedule recurring work. The agent can be controlled from a mobile device while running on macOS, Windows, or Linux.

stories.headline: The Price of Entry to the Frontier (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: The frontier AI market is sorting itself into closed camps as rationing programs and export limits decide who may run the strongest models. Enterprises are standardizing on one or two named vendors. Products are shipping with default models inside. Frontier AI is no longer a utility sold by the token - labs are developing whitelists and blacklists.

stories.headline: Agency and Agents (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Hugging Face Incident highlights AI agents' potential to self-organize and collaborate, bypassing set constraints to achieve common goals. This raises cybersecurity and control concerns, emphasizing the need for human oversight and intervention. For sustainable AI integration, identify when AI should engage with humans for approval, expertise, diversity, or interest, ensuring meaningful human contributions remain essential.

stories.headline: diffium-db: A live diff of what agents do to your database (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: diffium-db is a live TUI that shows users what is changing in their database as an agent, a migration, or anyone else works. Users just point it at a database, take a baseline, and leave it open. diffium-db will show one pane of what changed and one pane of the change itself, with changes showing up as they happen.

stories.headline: A Portable File Format for Agent Memory (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Memoryfields proposes storing agent memory as portable Markdown files with optional YAML metadata and a SQLite vector index. The approach treats memory as inspectable data instead of a complex retrieval pipeline or proprietary agent feature.

stories.headline: Google's Foundation Model for Zero-Shot Forecasting (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google has introduced TimesFM-3, a 330M-parameter time-series foundation model pretrained on more than 1 trillion time points. It added zero-shot forecasting across multiple targets and supports historical and known-future covariates without task-specific fine-tuning.

stories.headline: Product Manager, Applied AI at TLDR ($200k base + $60k bonus, Fully Remote)
stories.blurb: TLDR is hiring its first PM to help build the agent-first operating layer used across the company. We're looking for a builder who has shipped real products/systems with LLMs. Click here to learn more .

stories.headline: OpenAI has started letting some customers pay only when the AI works (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenAI has started testing an arrangement with a limited number of select major accounts where they only pay when the AI actually completes the job. The terms, customers, and prices are all unknown as OpenAI has not announced the test publicly. Token-based pricing has become a problem in the industry as it makes accounting difficult. The industry has started turning to outcome-based pricing as a market standard.

stories.headline: “Zlibrary my beloved”: Anthropic staff chats extolling piracy cited in Sony suit (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic's mass campaign of illegal torrenting allegedly began in July 2021. Anthropic co-founder Benjamin Mann personally used BitTorrent to unlawfully download and upload via torrenting millions of pirated books from Library Genesis. Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei allegedly approved the torrenting. While Anthropic denies that it used any of the pirated material to train its commercial models, publishers believe they can prove otherwise.

stories.headline: Department of War Launches OpenAI's ChatGPT Mil on GenAI.mil (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Department of War launched ChatGPT Mil on GenAI.mil for more than 3 million personnel.

stories.headline: ChatGPT Ads Reaches $1B Revenue Run Rate (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenAI said ChatGPT Ads reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate less than 200 days after launch.

stories.headline: Instinct Made the Consumer Agent Feel Real (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Instinct makes personal AI agents feel consumer-ready by combining memory, natural language, and real-world action across bookings, payments, and life admin.

stories.headline: ChatGPT and Reddit now face EU's toughest online safety rules (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox will face the EU's strictest Digital Services Act obligations after surpassing 45 million EU users.

stories.headline: Google develops AI Rooms for Gemini Enterprise (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google is prototyping "Rooms" for Gemini Enterprise, a workspace feature enabling teams to collaborate with Gemini on specific objectives.

digests.title: TLDR IT — 2026-09-01
digests.tagline: Microsoft 365 Goes Down 📉, Cursor Loses OpenAI 🤖, Tailscale Levels Up 🌐

stories.headline: Microsoft Exchange Online outage causes email failures, auth issues (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Microsoft spent Monday battling a widespread Microsoft 365 outage that started with Exchange Online and expanded to Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, Purview, and Defender XDR. Microsoft traced the disruption to a core authentication configuration problem and was rolling out mitigation across affected infrastructure, with users seeing gradual recovery by late Monday.

stories.headline: Cursor customers will lose access to OpenAI coding models in November (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenAI says it will stop providing its coding models to Cursor on November 12, giving customers roughly 10 weeks to switch models or platforms. Beyond Cursor, the bigger enterprise lesson is vendor dependency: model availability inside AI tools can change because of acquisitions, contracts, competition, or regulation, making multi-model support increasingly important.

stories.headline: Atlassian bets big on India as AI changes software development (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Atlassian is expanding its India development centre into a strategic R&D hub, with more than 2,700 employees and continued hiring planned across engineering and sales. AI agents are making software creation faster while shifting engineers' work toward directing agents, evaluating results, and applying human judgment to architecture, design, and product decisions.

stories.headline: Hackers claim millions of patient records stolen during data breach at healthcare giant McKesson (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: McKesson confirmed hackers breached several cloud-hosted accounts and stole data tied to its oncology, multispecialty, and medical-surgical businesses. ShinyHunters claims it used phishing and social engineering to gain access, stealing millions of rows from Snowflake and Salesforce containing personal and highly sensitive health information. The group reportedly demanded a $55 million ransom.

stories.headline: Why IT projects still fail (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: Even conventional IT initiatives continue to miss their goals: PMI says 31% of complex projects fail to deliver the full benefits originally intended. The article points to familiar culprits, unclear success metrics, weak business ownership, poor prioritization and under-resourcing, while arguing that AI can actually amplify these problems by accelerating output faster than organizations can review or absorb it.

stories.headline: The balkanization of virtualization will de-throne VMware, which doesn't mind a bit (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Broadcom's strategy will gradually end VMware's dominance of server virtualization as customers move workloads to alternatives, while VMware focuses on a smaller base of lucrative users adopting VMware Cloud Foundation. Three deadlines (November 22, 2026, March 31, 2027, and October 11, 2027) are expected to accelerate exits, although rivals generally acknowledge that VMware remains technically difficult to match.

stories.headline: Tailscale expands from VPN into a full connectivity platform (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Tailscale announced a broader connectivity platform at its Tailscale Up conference, extending its identity-based networking beyond VPN access into DNS filtering, privileged access management, AI agent controls, browser-based access, open-source networking, and developer APIs. Aperture, its AI gateway, reached general availability with guardrails, logging, model access, and integrations for provisioning and connecting to tailnet nodes.

stories.headline: Introducing data import for Microsoft OneDrive: An easier, faster, and higher-fidelity migration to Google Workspace (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google has made its advanced OneDrive migration tooling generally available directly in the Workspace Admin console at no additional cost. Admins can migrate multiple batches concurrently while preserving permissions, and a planning utility estimates source-data size and migration timelines before the move begins.

stories.headline: Next Generation Salesforce DevOps Center: Get Hands-On (27 minute read)
stories.blurb: Salesforce's Next Generation DevOps Center is now available natively in production instances, replacing the need for its managed package and adding AI-powered actions. This guide explains how to enable the app and move changes through its five-step workflow: creating a Work Item, committing changes, reviewing them, marking them ready, and promoting them through pipeline stages.

stories.headline: OpenTelemetry has graduated… now what? (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenTelemetry achieved CNCF graduated status in May, reflecting its production adoption, governance, security, API stability, documentation, and community health. Graduation confirms OpenTelemetry is production-ready and urges organizations that have not adopted it to do so, while highlighting continued work on AI workflows, browser and mobile observability, telemetry governance, packaging, and zero-code instrumentation.

stories.headline: Coming Aug 31st: AI-Powered Support Cases in Client VPN and Switches (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Meraki admins can now start Client VPN and switching support cases directly from the Dashboard's AI Assistant. The assistant analyzes the environment, suggests troubleshooting steps, and can generate a case summary for approval before sending it to Meraki support.

stories.headline: Network Subsystem (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: A practical deep dive that traces an IPv4/TCP packet over Ethernet through the Linux 7.1 network subsystem, from a network card to a server blocked in recv() and back out again.

stories.headline: Agent Package Manager for AI Azure Engineering (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Agent Package Manager (APM) is a dependency manager for AI agents that centralizes skills, prompts, instructions, plugins, and MCP servers in an apm.yml manifest.

stories.headline: Apple Adds Three More Macs to Obsolete Products List (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apple has moved the 2018 Retina MacBook Air and two 2017–2018 13-inch MacBook Pro models to its obsolete list.

digests.title: TLDR Web Dev — 2026-09-01
digests.tagline: Vercel designs with agents 🧑‍🎨, Macs for local LLMs 🖥, AI memory problems 💾

stories.headline: Autoscaling Lakebase Postgres (16 minute read)
stories.blurb: Neon uses Lakebase Postgres to enable real-time autoscaling of database resources, where compute sizes can change dynamically based on CPU load, memory use, and cache working set size without interrupting operations. This separation of storage and compute functions optimizes performance, reduces waste, and also allows for fast resource adjustments.

stories.headline: Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: A recent exploration shows that Claude Code Opus 5 in Auto Mode is vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, achieving a 60-80% success rate despite previous claims of a 0.00% success rate in these scenarios. The findings suggest that Auto Mode, which is intended as a safety measure, does not provide a definitive security guarantee.

stories.headline: How our agents build on-brand pages with design.md (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Vercel uses coding agents to create on-brand pages that adhere to specific design guidelines, using a public file called DESIGN.md to provide consistent design parameters for various tools and contexts. This framework incorporates a three-part system of guidance, a public stylesheet, and an evaluation loop to guarantee high-quality, cohesive outputs while continuously adapting through user feedback and real-world application.

stories.headline: Which Mac Should You Buy to Run Local LLMs in 2026? A Memory-First Buyer's Guide (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: When selecting a Mac for local LLMs in 2026, prioritize unified memory and memory bandwidth over chip type, as these factors impact model size and processing speed. The best choices vary by need: the Mac mini M4 Pro offers great value for 30B-class models, while the new M5 Max and Ultra models are great for heavy workloads requiring larger capacities.

stories.headline: AI-Written Code Is Still Your Code. Are You OK With That? (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI in software development is driving down the cost of writing code, but this might lead to a lack of understanding and ownership of the software created. As coding becomes increasingly automated, it raises important questions about the responsibilities of developers, particularly in areas like quality, security, and maintainability.

stories.headline: Your AGENTS.md is holding you back (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Context engineering has evolved from adding information to minimizing it, as overly detailed context can reduce AI agents' performance. To optimize AI agent functionality, it's recommended to regularly revise and test context documents, solicit feedback from the agents themselves, and maintain a detailed record of past errors to refine the context over time.

stories.headline: OpenClaw 2.0, Accidentally (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenClaw 2.0 has been released as the largest update in its history, with an overhaul of the installation process, browser experience, and collaborative functionalities.

stories.headline: FnScribe (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: FnScribe is a private dictation tool for macOS that transcribes voice recordings locally and integrates seamlessly with any active application. It allows users to dictate using a shortcut, supports hands-free operation, and offers features like smart cleanup and a personal dictionary.

stories.headline: DevSpace (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: DevSpace is a self-hosted server that integrates ChatGPT with local coding environments, allowing users to read, edit, and run code without exposing their files to third-party services. It enables ChatGPT to interact with users' projects directly, providing tools for repository inspection and command execution in a secure and controlled manner.

stories.headline: How to Build a Diffusion Language Model (34 minute read)
stories.blurb: Diffusion language models represent a new approach to generative AI, focusing on the simultaneous generation of entire text sequences rather than iteratively producing tokens one at a time. These models use techniques such as iterative refinement, variable-length generation, and error correction, allowing for faster and more controllable text generation.

stories.headline: I built a forgetting curve for an agent with one user (18 minute read)
stories.blurb: A forgetting curve was designed for a local-first vault agent to manage memory, but its complexity led to more problems than benefits. The system proposed intricate scoring and tiering for memory management, which ultimately went unused and overcomplicated the process of deciding what to retain. Simpler methods could effectively handle memory without the unnecessary layers of abstraction.

stories.headline: Instinct: Hottest Agentic Assistant – Payments Advantage? (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: Instinct uses SMS and voice communication to manage consumer tasks across various sectors without a traditional eCommerce interface, showing a shift toward agentic commerce in everyday services.

stories.headline: AI memory lock-in works until it blocks your own product (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI memory lock-in improves user retention by accumulating context that makes switching expensive, but it can also hurt product adoption within a company's own offerings.

stories.headline: The Safest Job from AI may be Writing (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: Despite advancements in AI-generated content, human writing remains safe from obsolescence as AI struggles to capture the depth, authenticity, and subjectivity inherent in effective prose.

stories.headline: Agent memory as a file format (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: Memoryfields represent a simplified and effective data format for agent memory, allowing AI agents to store and retrieve relevant information through directly written Markdown pages and semantic search, rather than relying on complex multi-stage memory systems.

digests.title: TLDR InfoSec — 2026-09-01
digests.tagline: Anthropic Notifies Hacked Users 📢, OSINT Prompt Injections 😈, Universal Android PrivEsc 🤖

stories.headline: ShinyHunters Claims it Stole 284 Million Patient Records from McKesson (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: McKesson detected an intrusion on August 25 tied to third-party apps in its Oncology & Multispecialty and Medical-Surgical units. ShinyHunters vished McKesson employees, hijacked Okta SSO accounts, then pulled roughly a terabyte from Salesforce and Snowflake over four days. The group demanded $55,236,150 with a 72-hour deadline, which McKesson didn't pay. Breached data includes 284 million records containing SSNs, birth dates, Medicaid info, medical record numbers, medication/allergy data, and employee records.

stories.headline: Critical Microsoft UFO MCP Flaw Lets Attackers Remotely Control Android Devices Without Authentication (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Unauthenticated attackers can drive ADB commands on Android devices connected to Microsoft's open-source UFO Desktop AgentOS through CVE-2026-73296, which affects versions up to v3.0.7 and has no official patch. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability to capture screenshots, extract UI hierarchy data, and tap, swipe, and text-entry actions on TCP 8020 and 8021 whenever operators follow the documented remote-deployment guidance and bind to 0.0.0.0. Users should restrict those ports to trusted hosts and front the services with TLS and an authenticated reverse proxy until the proposed UFO_MCP_API_KEY bearer-token fix merges.

stories.headline: Anthropic Warns Claude Users of Infostealer Malware Infections (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic warned affected Claude users that infostealers hijacked browser sessions and drained usage limits. The malware included Vidar, Lumma, StealC, RedLine, Acreed, and AMOS. Anthropic logged out compromised sessions, removed stored payment methods, and refunded identified unauthorized charges. Users should remove malware before re-adding payment details.

stories.headline: When the Source Attacks Back: Prompt Injection Is Coming for OSINT (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: Security researcher Dekens has demonstrated how adversaries can manipulate AI-assisted OSINT investigations by planting hidden prompt injections within digital documents. Through a dedicated training lab, Dekens highlights techniques like pushing CSS div elements off-screen, embedding white-on-white text in PDFs, and hiding instructions in unformatted spreadsheet cells. While not yet observed in active campaigns, these invisible artifacts successfully steer language models toward false narratives without altering the visually rendered file. To defend against poisoned sources, investigators should hash original documents and independently extract text using tools like Apache Tika or Tesseract to compare against the visual output. Furthermore, analysts must strictly isolate AI models in read-only environments to prevent untrusted inputs from executing unauthorized actions.

stories.headline: Philippine Nuclear Agency and Naval Contractor Targeted by Suspected Chinese-Speaking Operator Using Known Vulnerabilities (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Researchers found an exposed Amsterdam server staging tools and stolen Philippine data. Custom scripts abused ownCloud CVE-2023-49105, impersonating known users through unsigned WebDAV URLs. The recovered data included reactor records, radiation-safety files, employee PII, travel documents, BitLocker keys, KeePass data, and AxCrypt files. Logs referenced roughly 9 GB taken from the nuclear agency. A naval contractor's WordPress site was breached through LiteSpeed Cache CVE-2024-28000 and XML-RPC password guessing. The server also hosted Sliver, Metasploit, Mettle, and a loader that fetched a second-stage payload.

stories.headline: When it Snows it Pours – Anatomy of a ServiceNow Red Team (19 minute read)
stories.blurb: MDSec red-team engagements turned phished ServiceNow users, exposed MID config.xml files, and over-permissioned roles into tenant admin access. Roles including catalog_admin, import_admin, and sn_cmdb_editor enabled Glide-script execution or role chaining. Operators created hidden admin accounts, altered timestamps, removed login and role histories, and used scheduled jobs as SnowFall C2 callbacks. From the tenant, they enumerated incidents and attachments, extracted credentials, bypassed adaptive authentication, and executed commands on MID servers through JAR plugins or the ECC queue.

stories.headline: Cloudflare OS (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Cloudflare OS is an “operating system” for AI productivity that consists of an agent chat UI, a sandboxed application development environment for small personal apps, and security guardrails.

stories.headline: EMBA (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: EMBA is designed as the central firmware analysis and SBOM tool for penetration testers, product security teams, developers, and responsible product managers. It supports the complete security analysis process, starting with firmware extraction, doing static analysis and dynamic analysis via emulation, building the SBOM, and finally generating a web-based vulnerability report.

stories.headline: Introducing Adaptive Intelligence: Undermining the Economics of Every Bot Attack (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cloudflare has launched Adaptive Intelligence, a bot detection engine designed to make evasion economically unviable for attackers by continuously retraining its models on live traffic. Rather than relying on deterministic rules, the engine utilizes non-deterministic signal weighting and delayed reactions to prevent threat actors from isolating and defeating specific defenses. This cross-temporal evaluation allows the system to detect slow credential-stuffing attacks distributed across residential proxies that would otherwise bypass standard rate limits. Enterprise customers can activate the continuous retraining component immediately by enabling "Auto Update Machine Learning" in their Bot Management dashboard, while advanced features such as disposable rule generation are still in development.

stories.headline: Open-Source Post-Quantum Cryptography Serverless CA (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Paul Schwarzenberger updated his open-source serverless CA with support for ML-DSA post-quantum cryptography. CA private keys are generated and used within AWS KMS FIPS 140-3 HSMS. ML-DSA is still not universally supported by applications, so users should check compatibility before adopting.

stories.headline: How AI Builders Will Get Hacked (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Developers who are frequently building tools with AI should ensure that they have a continuously running system that maintains a list of publicly exposed systems and continuously probes for basic security properties. AI builders can consider using full harnesses to comprehensively test critical systems. With the velocity of AI development, losing track of dangling, public resources will become a key attack vector.

stories.headline: OEMpocalypse Now (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Calif researcher Lukas Maar has developed a universal exploitation strategy that elevates an unprivileged Android app to root across modern Samsung, Xiaomi, and Oppo devices. Rather than hunting for generic kernel or chipset vulnerabilities, Maar targeted the proprietary OEM software overlays, such as One UI and HyperOS, that span each vendor's entire device lineup. The exploit leverages a page use-after-free vulnerability mapped to a freed physical page. This reliable technique successfully bypasses KASLR, control-flow hijacking, and slab protections without modification across kernels 5.4 through 6.12. While this initial publication outlines the overarching methodology on locked bootloaders, Maar plans to release the specific exploit chains affecting July 2026 flagship devices like the Galaxy S26 Ultra in future installments.

stories.headline: Update on recent cybersecurity incident (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Boston Scientific detected a cyber incident on August 25 that disrupted on-premises operating systems and business applications.

stories.headline: Data Security Incident - 27.08.26 (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Manchester Airports Group says an unauthorized party obtained booking and Wi‑Fi signup data from Manchester, Stansted, and East Midlands airports.

digests.title: TLDR Design — 2026-09-01
digests.tagline: Instagram AI Crack Down 🤖, No Apple Watch Redesign ⌚, Alibaba Video Maker 🎬

stories.headline: A redesigned Apple Watch now seems further in the future (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apple's Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected to be modest upgrades focused on new ceramic case options and improved health tracking, including continuous heart-rate monitoring and more insightful wellness software, while a major redesign remains in development and could arrive in 2027 or be delayed until 2028.

stories.headline: Alibaba Launches Wan3.0 AI Video Model after $10 Billion Share Sale (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Alibaba officially rolled out Wan3.0, an upgraded AI video-generation model, a day after announcing a $10 billion share placement to fund rising AI spending. The model generates 30-second videos from documents, spreadsheets, slides, and web pages, and has been used since its August 6 public beta. The share sale is the largest-ever primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company, coming after Alibaba reported a 75% plunge in quarterly earnings due to soaring AI capital expenditure.

stories.headline: Instagram Will Demote AI-generated Influencers if They Don't Clearly Label Their Account (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Instagram now requires profiles featuring AI-generated personas to use a new "AI-generated profile" label, replacing the previous optional "AI creator" tag. Accounts that don't apply the label to AI-generated people will face reduced reach, though appeals are possible through the Account Status dashboard. The change targets only AI persona accounts specifically, not broader AI-generated content, amid rising concern over misleading AI "influencers" impersonating real humans.

stories.headline: Workflow Lab: Moving between Design and Code with Agents (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Figma's MCP server and Code Connect give coding agents access to a team's components, tokens, and layouts, so generated code matches design specs. In the example workflow, a developer diagrams the flow in FigJam, reuses existing components, and catches token drift before review.

stories.headline: How AI-Ready is Your Design System? Now You Can Measure It. (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: open-design-system-bench is an open benchmark measuring whether AI coding agents use a design system correctly when generating UI. Four systems scored between 52.2 and 63.4 on its AI-readiness composite, and none reached the AI-native tier. Across 898 graded generations, some models ignored the design system entirely while others hallucinated component names.

stories.headline: The Custodial Era of UX: Cleaning Up After AI (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI is pushing UX into a “custodial era” where teams can generate and ship features faster than they can properly evaluate them, creating UX debt. As a result, UX practitioners increasingly act as custodians who clean up, simplify, validate, and triage AI-generated experiences, helping organizations distinguish what can be built from what should be built, while adapting research and evaluation processes to keep pace with rapid production and embedding UX principles directly into AI generation workflows to prevent future problems.

stories.headline: Build a Reusable Web Scraper from One Prompt (Website)
stories.blurb: BrowserAct builds and verifies a reusable scraper on a live website, then runs it whenever you need fresh results.

stories.headline: Build Your iPhone App (Website)
stories.blurb: x1 helps builders turn app ideas into working iPhone apps through guided planning, visual design, milestone-based building, QA, publishing prep, and iteration.

stories.headline: App Store Screenshot Design Inspiration (Website)
stories.blurb: Browse curated App Store screenshots, paywalls, onboarding flows, and icons from the best-designed iOS apps.

stories.headline: Two Adobe AI Features Worth a Web Designer's Attention (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Adobe added a conversational AI Assistant to Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere, and Frame.io in June 2026, automating multi-step production tasks like batch resizing and background removal. Illustrator's Text to Vector tool generates genuinely editable SVG paths rather than raster images, a capability no major competing AI tool offers.

stories.headline: The new CD Projekt Red logo just sparked the weirdest backlash graphic design has ever seen (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: CD Projekt Red has refreshed its firebird logo with sharper, more aggressive features and a stronger use of red to better reflect the mythological Slavic raróg it represents, but despite the redesign being a relatively modest evolution, some social media users have bizarrely interpreted the shift to a black-and-red color scheme as a political statement, even though the company says the update is simply intended to create a more modern, confident, energetic, and culturally authentic brand identity.

stories.headline: Design's Legibility Gap (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Design's struggle for legitimacy stems from "legibility," where organizations only value predictable, determinate work they can measure and plan around. Unlike engineering or marketing, UX/Design remained a synthetic, indeterminate practice, making its core work—research, iteration, and conceptual modeling—invisible to organizations. Design leadership's real challenge, then, is not translating design to the business, but expanding what businesses recognize as legitimate, valuable work.

stories.headline: Moriz Oberberger's bendy figures and whimsical cartoons reveal “the strange beauty of ordinary situations” (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Illustrator and animator Moriz Oberberger creates playful yet subtly unsettling artwork featuring awkward characters, unusual proportions, and expressive mark-making, using experimental drawing and painting techniques to explore vulnerability, tension, and the strange beauty hidden within everyday situations.

stories.headline: Nope, the new Apple Mac mini ad isn't AI – and there's a delightful BTS video to prove it (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apple's new Mac mini stop-motion ad celebrates human craftsmanship with handmade clay animation, positioning the computer as a tool that enhances rather than replaces creativity.

stories.headline: This Rebrand of a Voice-Journaling App Looks Lovely, but is an 'AI Illustration System' the Right Call? (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Working Assembly's new identity for voice-journaling app Untold centers on a bespoke AI illustration system trained to feel emotionally resonant rather than algorithmically generated.
